key_insight: An integer fluxonium can turn dominant leakage from the logical |f⟩ state into detectable erasures, enabling hardware-efficient error detection and conversion.
engineering_relevance: The approach uses the qubit’s native level structure and existing readout resonator to support mid-circuit erasure checks with lower gate error and longer effective lifetimes, which is valuable for scalable quantum error correction.
method: Encode logical states in |g⟩ and |f⟩, with |e⟩ serving as an erasure flag.
Exploit suppressed |f⟩→|g⟩ transitions and convert dominant |f⟩→|e⟩ events into detectable erasures.
Use a design regime that cancels the logical-state frequency shift, enabling ancilla-free mid-circuit checks with the readout resonator.
evidence_signal: Discarding detected erasures produced an 8.4× increase in |f⟩ lifetime, a 1.38× increase in Hahn-echo time, and reduced single-qubit gate error from 0.061(2)% to 0.030(5)%.
watch_item: The results still require improved erasure bias and hardware refinement to realize a fully effective erasure qubit at scale.
paper_title: Hardware-efficient erasure-error detection with an integer fluxonium
